newsitem.title: FINLAND: Raisio says Benecol sales rose in Nov-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Raisio says Benecol sales rose in Nov-Feb.

text.p: Finnish food, chemicals and animal feed group Raisio Tehtaat Oy said on Thursday sales of its Benecol cholesterol-cutting margarine had picked up considerably in November-February, but gave no details.
"Sales in November-February have developed considerably due to the better availability of the raw material," said Jukka Kaitaranta head of Raisio's Benecol unit.
"And deliveries to retailers have improved," he added.
Kaitaranta said new capacity and increased availability of the raw material had improved conditions for Benecol production.
"Production-wise we are in a good situation," he said.
A new manufacturing plant for the active ingredient in Benecol came on stream at the end of last year.
The margarine is currently available only in Finland: Raisio plans to start exporting it to Sweden next year, but CEO Matti Salminen declined to specify the timetable.
"It would be a natural step to launch Benecol to Sweden, Salminen said, adding "Our market share in Sweden (in margarines) is now 36 percent."
Raisio bought a 77.5 percent stake in Swedish margarine maker Carlsham Mejeri Ab in October.
